scenario: TikTok 广告后端面试,被问「campaign 设置为什么用关系型库而不是 NoSQL」。她卡成「Relational data model and relational data, okay okay」,然后开始罗列字段,不给拍板理由。
scenario_en: In the TikTok ads backend interview she's asked why she chose a relational DB over NoSQL for campaign settings. She echoes "relational data model and relational data, okay okay" and lists fields without a deciding reason.
q: 「为什么选关系型而不是 NoSQL」怎么一句给出决定性理由?
q_en: How do you give the deciding reason for "relational over NoSQL" in one line?
options: We use the relational data model and relational data, so campaign type, ROI goal, budget — it's all relational, so it made sense to me.
So, NoSQL could also work, but relational is also fine, there are some tradeoffs, so, let me think, I'd say it just fit better somehow.
I went relational over NoSQL because the settings were highly relational and needed joins. That costs easy horizontal scaling — fine at our write volume.
When selecting a database one must weigh consistency, scalability, and the data model, since relational systems provide ACID guarantees and referential integrity throughout.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「X over Y because 约束 Z, 代价 W」拍板 vs 罗列字段+「it made sense」never justifies。
why: 把决定压成「X over Y because 约束 Z; 代价 W, 可接受因为…」。她的毛病是罗列字段加「it made sense」,不给决定性理由。
why_en: Say "relational over NoSQL because the data was relational and needed joins; the cost is scaling, which was fine" — don't just say it made sense.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只想确认你知道两种库的区别、还没到定型阶段,先并列讲差异、暂不拍板也可以。

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库:用表和外键存结构化数据,支持 join 和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relational database stores structured data in tables with foreign keys, supporting joins and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型库:文档/键值等模型,弱化关系换更易水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL databases use document or key-value models, trading relations for easier horizontal scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接:按外键把多张表拼到一起查询。

termDefinitions.meaning: 水平扩展:靠加机器分担负载,而不是升单机配置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling adds more machines to share load instead of enlarging one server.

scenario: TikTok 广告后端面试,被问「campaign creation 为什么走同步 REST 而不是异步消息队列」。她说「I integrate the backend API… what I usually do is align the API」绕开了理由。
scenario_en: In the TikTok ads backend interview she's asked why campaign creation uses a synchronous REST call instead of an async queue. She drifts into "I integrate the backend API... I align the API" and skips the reason.
q: 「为什么用同步而不是异步」怎么一句给出决定性理由?
q_en: How do you give the deciding reason for "synchronous over async" in one line?
options: We kept creation synchronous because the advertiser needs an immediate success-or-error on submit. Async would decouple load, but that costs instant feedback — not worth it.
We go the sync way, not the async way, because the user submit and then the read pass is faster, so it feel more real-time to them.
So, a queue could help with load, but sync is also okay, and, hmm, there are pros and cons, so I'd say we just went with what was simpler.
Synchronous and asynchronous communication each present distinct tradeoffs in coupling, latency, and throughput that architects must carefully evaluate before deciding on either one.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「sync because 即时反馈, async 省耦合但代价 W」vs「read pass」错词加绕开理由。

why_en: Say "sync because the advertiser needs instant success or error; async would cut coupling but costs that feedback" — don't drift into aligning the API.
whenOtherWins: 如果创建是重后台作业、用户并不等结果,那选异步队列、接受延迟反馈反而更对。

scenario: TikTok 广告面试,被问「ROI 看板数字为什么预计算缓存,而不是每次实时算」。她说「I watch the dashboard and use some query to check」,没答到选型理由。

q: 「为什么预计算缓存而不是实时算」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "precompute-and-cache over compute-on-read" in one line?
options: So, real-time would be more fresh, but caching is faster, and, um, both have tradeoffs, so, I think we just picked the one that felt faster.
We do pre-compute, because real-time compute is too slow when the row is many, and the number they don't change so fast, so cache is better.
Caching introduces a well-known tradeoff between data freshness and read latency that engineers should always weigh against the volatility of the underlying data source.
We precompute because reads far outnumber writes and the numbers update hourly. Live compute would be fresher, but that costs latency we didn't need to pay.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「cache because 读多写少, 代价新鲜度」拍板 vs Chinglish 语法加不落到理由。
why: 把决定压成「缓存 because 读远多于写加小时级更新; 实时更新鲜但代价是延迟」。她的毛病是讲操作、不给选型理由。
why_en: Say "cache because reads dwarf writes and data updates hourly; live compute is fresher but costs latency" — don't just describe watching the dashboard.
whenOtherWins: 如果数字要秒级最新、读也不算多,那选实时计算、接受更高延迟才对。

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计算:提前算好结果存起来,查询时直接取,不再现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precompute means calculating results ahead of time and storing them, so reads fetch instead of recomputing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时计算:每次请求现场算,数据最新但每次都付计算延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compute-on-read calculates on every request — freshest data, but you pay the compute latency each time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存:把热数据放在快存储里,读得更快,代价是可能过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache keeps hot data in fast storage for quicker reads, at the cost of possible staleness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新鲜度:数据距离最新状态有多近,缓存越久越可能过时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Freshness is how close the data is to its latest state; the longer it's cached, the staler it can get.

scenario: 后端 workflow 迁移面试,被问「为什么用灰度分批上线,而不是一次性切换」。她卡成「the migration takes some time, but…」,没说清选型。
scenario_en: In a backend workflow migration interview she's asked why she chose a gradual, staged rollout over a one-shot cutover. She stalls on "the migration takes some time, but..." and never states the reason.
q: 「为什么灰度分批而不是一次性切」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "gradual rollout over big-bang cutover" in one line?
options: A phased rollout and a big-bang cutover differ chiefly in blast radius and rollback cost, which any migration plan should carefully account for before execution begins.
I chose a staged rollout because it was a live production system, so I wanted a small blast radius. It's slower to finish, an acceptable price for safety.
We do the migration step by step, not one time, because if it break, the roll back pass is easier, and, so so, it's more safe for us.
So, one shot is faster, but step by step is safer, there are tradeoffs, so, let me think how to say, we kind of just went slower.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「staged because 小 blast radius, 代价更慢」vs「roll back pass」错词加绕。
why: 把决定压成「灰度 because 线上系统要小 blast radius; 更慢但为安全值得」。她的毛病是卡在「takes some time」,不给理由。
why_en: Say "staged because it was live, I wanted a small blast radius; it's slower but that's an acceptable price for safety" — don't stall on "takes some time".
whenOtherWins: 如果是全新系统、没线上流量、坏了也不影响用户,那一次性切、图快也合理。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次性切换:所有流量同时切到新系统,快但坏了全体受影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A big-bang cutover switches all traffic to the new system at once — fast, but any failure hits everyone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 影响半径:一次故障最多波及多少用户或系统。

termDefinitions.meaning: 回滚:出问题时把系统退回上一个正常版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rollback reverts the system to the last good version when something goes wrong.

options: So, a new table would be cleaner, but reusing is also fine, and, hmm, both work, so I'd say we just added it to what we had.
We add the column to the old table, not build new table, because the data model already have the campaign, so it more easy to join.
I extended the existing table because Promotion Days shared the campaign's timeline and I needed one query. That risks a wider row, which stayed manageable.
Schema evolution presents a classic tradeoff between normalization and query simplicity, and the decision ultimately hinges on access patterns and future maintainability concerns.

scenario: 预算自动化面试,被问「并发改预算为什么用乐观锁而不是悲观锁」。她说「the budget setting… I need to think about the scale」,没答到锁的选型。
scenario_en: In the budget-automation interview she's asked why she chose optimistic locking over pessimistic locking for concurrent budget edits. She says "the budget setting... I need to think about the scale" and misses the reason.
q: 「为什么乐观锁而不是悲观锁」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "optimistic over pessimistic locking" in one line?
options: I used optimistic locking because conflicts on the same budget were rare, so I didn't want to hold a lock. The cost is occasional retries, which were cheap here.
We use the optimistic lock, not pessimistic lock, because most time no conflict, so we don't need to lock every write pass, it more fast.
So, pessimistic is safer, but optimistic is lighter, there are tradeoffs, um, so we just picked the lighter one I think.
Optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control differ mainly in how they handle contention, and the right choice depends on the expected conflict rate within the workload.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「乐观锁 because 冲突少, 代价重试」vs「write pass」错词加跑题到 scale。
why: 把决定压成「乐观锁 because 冲突罕见、不想持锁; 代价是偶尔重试, 便宜」。她的毛病是跳到 scale、不答锁的选型。
why_en: Say "optimistic because conflicts were rare so I didn't want to hold a lock; the cost is occasional retries, which were cheap" — don't jump to scale.
whenOtherWins: 如果同一预算高频并发写、冲突常见,那悲观锁避免大量重试反而更划算。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the route a write request travels; she often misspeaks it as "write pass".

scenario: 预算自动化面试,被问「调度这块为什么自己实现,而不是接现成组件」。她绕到团队分工,没答 build-vs-buy 的理由。
scenario_en: In the budget-automation interview she's asked why she chose to build the scheduling in-house instead of adopting an existing component. She drifts into team structure and never answers the build-vs-buy reason.
q: 「为什么自建而不是用现成的」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "build in-house over adopting an existing component" in one line?
options: We build it self, not use the ready one, because our logic is special, the ready one can not fit, so so, we have to do our own.
Build-versus-buy decisions weigh engineering cost against control and fit, and teams should evaluate whether an off-the-shelf solution meets their specific requirements first.
So, buying is faster, but building gives control, both have tradeoffs, and, let me think, we kind of just built it ourselves.
I built it because our budget rules were too custom for any off-the-shelf tool to fit. That costs more maintenance, accepted since the logic was core.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「自建 because 太定制, 代价维护」拍板 vs「build it self」Chinglish 加绕分工。
why: 把决定压成「自建 because 逻辑太定制、现成的不合; 代价是更多维护, 因核心而值得」。她的毛病是绕到分工、不给理由。
why_en: Say "built it because the rules were too custom for any off-the-shelf tool; the cost is more maintenance, accepted since it was core" — don't drift to team structure.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求很通用、现成组件基本能覆盖,那直接用现成的、省下维护成本更明智。

Build-versus-buy decisions weigh engineering cost against control and fit, and teams should evaluate whether an off-the-shelf solution meets their specific requirements first.
So, buying is faster, but building gives control, both have tradeoffs, and, let me think, we kind of just built it ourselves.
I built it because our budget rules were too custom for any off-the-shelf tool to fit. That costs more maintenance, accepted since the logic was core.

选项主张:背 build-vs-buy 的教科书框架。

termDefinitions.meaning: 自建还是采购:自己写还是用现成方案的取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Build vs buy is the tradeoff between writing something yourself and adopting an existing solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 现成组件:开箱即用的第三方或开源方案,快但未必贴合需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Off-the-shelf means a ready-made third-party or open-source solution — fast, but not always a perfect fit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自建:团队自己开发维护,更贴合但要承担维护成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-house means the team builds and maintains it themselves — better fit, but you own the maintenance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护成本:上线后持续修 bug、升级、运维要付出的长期投入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Maintenance cost is the ongoing effort of fixing, upgrading, and operating something after it ships.

scenario: 面试被问「为什么一开始就和其他后端定死 API 契约,而不是先各写各的再对齐」。她重复「align the API constructs with other backend engineers」,没给理由。
scenario_en: She's asked why she chose to lock the API contract with other backend engineers up front instead of each side building first and reconciling later. She repeats "align the API constructs with other backend engineers" with no reason.
q: 「为什么一开始就定死 API 契约」怎么一句拍板?
q_en: How do you commit to "lock the API contract up front" in one line?
options: So, we could also align later, but early is also fine, there are tradeoffs both ways, so we just agreed on it early I guess.
I locked the contract early because both sides were building in parallel, so a mismatch would block us. That costs some upfront design time, well worth it.
We align the API construct early, not later, because if not, the two side will not match, and then the integrate pass will break.
Defining an API contract early versus iterating later is a coordination tradeoff, and the decision depends on team parallelism and the cost of downstream integration rework.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳:一句「早定 because 并行会 block, 代价前期时间」vs「integrate pass」错词加重复原话。
why: 把决定压成「早定契约 because 双方并行、不对齐会互相 block; 代价是前期设计时间, 值得」。她的毛病是重复「align the API」不给理由。
why_en: Say "locked it early because both sides built in parallel and a mismatch would block us; the cost is upfront design time, well worth it" — don't just repeat aligning the API.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有你一个人开发、没有并行方,那先各写各的、后期再对齐反而更灵活。

termDefinitions.meaning: API 契约:双方约定好的接口格式,字段、类型、返回都定死。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API contract is the agreed interface shape — fields, types, and responses both sides commit to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行开发:多方同时各自开发,靠契约保证最后能对上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Parallel development means several sides build at the same time, relying on a contract to fit together later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 阻塞依赖:一方没就绪,另一方就卡住动不了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking dependency is when one side can't proceed until another is ready.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成:把各方独立开发的部分拼到一起联调。她常误说「integrate pass」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integration is joining independently built parts and getting them to work together; she misspeaks it as "integrate pass".
